decision.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to keep its target for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Economic growth appears to have been moderate during the first half of this year, despite the ongoing adjustment in the housing sector.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that economic growth appears moderate despite ongoing adjustments in the housing sector.

changes.quote: Readings on core inflation have improved modestly in recent months.
changes.explanation: A new addition acknowledges that core inflation readings showed modest improvement recently.

changes.quote: However, a sustained moderation in inflation pressures has yet to be convincingly demonstrated.
changes.explanation: The Fed added this caution to signal that lower inflation needs to be proven over time before they change rates.
This sentence was removed from the previous statement.

tone_quotes.quote: However, a sustained moderation in inflation pressures has yet to be convincingly demonstrated.
In these circumstances, the Committee's predominant policy concern remains the risk that inflation will fail to moderate as expected.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 13.41% APR costs about $55.88 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 5.15% and moved -1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.53% would fall by about $1.98 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.4%, and employers added an average of 144k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.7% over the past year (May 2007); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.1%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 1.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -4 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.08% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that future decisions will depend entirely on incoming data regarding inflation and growth. An educational forecast model gives the next meeting a 59% chance of a hold, a 4% chance of a cut, and a 37% chance of a hike.
